samples.question: The picture is filled with two overlapping families of straight dark lines on a plain pale background. Inside one family every line is parallel to the others, the lines are evenly spaced and all have the same thickness; the two families differ in tilt and in spacing, and every line of both families is painted in the same dark colour, so no single line is marked out. Where lines of the two families fall on top of one another more pale background stays visible, and where they fall between one another the dark ink packs together, so the picture as a whole is crossed by broad pale and dark bands that are many times wider than the spacing of either family. Those broad bands are parallel to one another and are not drawn as lines anywhere: no painted line runs along them, and neither line family runs within 22 degrees of the band direction. The tilt of either line family, the spacing of the lines, their thickness, the amount of ink and the position of the pattern carry no information about the answer. The broad bands run within 7 degrees of one of four directions: horizontal (left to right), vertical (top to bottom), rising (from the bottom left towards the top right) or falling (from the top left towards the bottom right). In which direction do the broad bands run? Answer horizontal, vertical, rising or falling.
